title: CUDA
content:
CUDA is NVIDIA's proprietary platform for programming GPUs, consisting of a kernel language (C++), a driver for hardware management, and a runtime API for launching kernels. Every inference engine, framework, and library in the NVIDIA ecosystem depends on CUDA, including cuBLAS — NVIDIA's optimized implementation of standard linear algebra routines and the default backend for matrix multiplications in most inference pipelines. Understanding CUDA is the foundation for diagnosing performance problems that tools and engines cannot solve automatically.

Visit the following resources to learn more:

- [@official@CUDA Programming Guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/)
- [@official@cuBLAS Documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cublas/)
- [@official@An Even Easier Introduction to CUDA (Updated)](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/even-easier-introduction-cuda/)
- [@video@CUDA Programming Course – High-Performance Computing with GPUs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=86FAWCzIe_4)
